what: Edit PDF Text lets you change words that are already in a PDF. The page is shown on screen with each line of text inside a blue box. You click a box, type the new text, and save a new PDF with your changes.

It is made for small fixes: a typo, a wrong date, a misspelled name, an old phone number or a price. It covers the old line with the page color behind it and writes your new text in the same place, size and color. Where the PDF holds the letters you need, it reuses the PDF’s own font so the change blends in.
If a page is a scan, the tool tries to read the English text from the picture so you can still click and change lines. Everything runs in your browser, and the file is not uploaded.
uses: Correct a spelling mistake in a finished PDF when you no longer have the original Word file.
Change the date, invoice number or amount on a document you reuse.
Fix a misspelled name or an old address on a letter or certificate draft.
Clear the text of a line completely to blank it out on the page.
Change text on a scanned page
On a scanned English page, the tool reads the text so you can change a line, written in a standard font.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a PDF here" or drag a PDF onto the box. The editor opens and shows page 1. Above the page you see "Page 1 of N", two arrow buttons and the counter "No changes yet".
Find the line you want to change

Each line or run of text has a blue box over it. Use the "‹" and "›" buttons to move to other pages. A note above the page tells you what to do, or tells you if the page is a scan or has no editable text.
Click or tap a blue box, or select it with the keyboard and press Enter. An edit bar appears below the page with the current text already selected in the input box.

Type your new text. The page updates as you type, so you can see how it fits. The counter above the page changes to "1 line changed", "2 lines changed" and so on. To clear a line completely, delete all its text.
Press "Done" or the Enter key to close the edit bar. Press "Undo" to put that line back to its original text. You can then click another blue box.
Move between pages with the arrows. Your changes on every page are kept until you save.
The button becomes active once at least one line is changed. A message tells you how many changes were saved and whether they used the PDF’s own font or the closest standard font.
Click "Download PDF". The new file is named like letter-edited.pdf. Your original file is not changed.
features: Every line of real text gets its own clickable blue box.
Keeps the original font when possible
If the PDF carries its own font and that font has every letter you type, your text is written in that same font.
Otherwise the closest standard font is used: Helvetica, Times or Courier, with matching bold and italic.
The tool samples the page to find the background and text colors, and writes the new text at the same spot and size.
On scanned pages with English text, built-in OCR finds the lines so you can edit them. A progress bar shows the reading progress.
Change lines on several pages and save them all in one file.
See how many lines you changed, and undo any single line.

example.title: Worked example: fixing a date on a letter
example.text: Nadia has a 2-page letter.pdf where page 1 says "Date: 3 March 2025" but it should be 2026. She loads the file, clicks the blue box around that line and changes 2025 to 2026. The counter shows "1 line changed". She clicks "Done", then "Save edited PDF". The message says the change was saved in the original font, because all the digits she typed already exist in the PDF’s font. She downloads letter-edited.pdf.

tips: Keep new text about the same length as the old text. Longer text is not wrapped and can run past the original line.
Each blue box is one run of text, which may be a whole line or just part of it. Edit the box that holds the words you want.
The old text is covered, not removed from the file. Do not use this tool to hide private information, because the old words may still be found by copying or searching.
If the page background has a pattern or a photo, the cover patch is a flat color and may be visible. Plain white pages give the best result.
Rotated or mirrored text cannot be edited, and scan reading only works for English text on pages that are not rotated.
Open the downloaded file and check every change before you send it.
problems: The note says "This page has no text that can be edited"
The page has no real text and is rotated, so it cannot be read. Try straightening it with Rotate PDF first, then edit the new file.
The note says "No text could be read on this page"
The scan may be handwriting, a photo, a language other than English, or too blurry. This tool cannot edit that page.
A message says some letters cannot be written into the PDF
The PDF’s own font does not have those letters, and the standard fonts only support Latin letters. Remove characters from other scripts or special symbols.
The new text is in a slightly different font
The PDF did not contain every letter you typed in its own font, so the closest standard font was used. Try wording that reuses letters already in the line, or accept the close match.
A message says "This PDF is password protected"
Remove the password in a PDF reader that knows it, save a copy, and edit that copy.
